result.title: Stop or Clarify? Experience-Conditioned Active Fact Verification
result.summary: Fact-verification benchmarks score the final label, while an interactive verifier must first decide whether the available evidence is sufficient. We focus on that intermediate Stop-or-Clarify Decision. Uncertainty alone is insufficient, because the benefit of another evidence-acquisition step is unknown before the step is taken. Sequential Experience-Adaptive Clarification (SEAC) wraps a fixed verifier with a lightweight evidence-acquisition policy. For each claim, SEAC retrieves evidence, runs the verifier, forms a label-free decision state, and combines stop risk with an observational clarification-utility estimate from earlier executed trajectories. Clarification is requested only when this score exceeds the action cost and decision threshold. On SciFact, LIAR, and FEVER, SEAC improves mean accuracy and macro-F1 over the compared fact-verification and active-retrieval baselines. Equal-budget and formula-level diagnostics support selective clarification as a contributor to the gain, while the small SciFact split leaves its paired improvement inconclusive.

AI.brief_summary: 研究交互式事实核查中的「停止或澄清」决策，提出 SEAC 在固定验证器外包裹轻量证据获取策略：由无标签决策状态结合停止风险与历史轨迹中的澄清效用估计，仅在得分超过动作成本与阈值时继续检索。
AI.relevance_reason: 其经验条件化的澄清效用估计与成本—阈值权衡，可为 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 的收益成本判断和停止策略提供可核查线索；但工作属纯文本事实核查，未涉及视觉状态表示。
